title: Everyday Local News
description: Ten short news stories, letters and diary entries from a small American town: a new bus line, an ice storm, a science prize, a lost dog, the harvest festival, a new hospital wing, the old mill, school lunches, summer reading and a new stadium.

lessons.title: A New Bus Line
lessons.summary: A new electric bus line connects the train station, the hospital and the high school.
lessons.text:
On Monday morning, a new bus line started in Greenfield. The Number 9 bus connects the train station with the hospital, the high school and the shopping center. Before the new line, there was no bus between these places, so people had to drive or walk.

The new buses are small, quiet and clean. Each bus has an electric motor, so it produces zero smoke. "An electric motor is quieter than a normal one," said Karen Lee, who is in charge of the town's buses. "And zero smoke is good for everyone, especially in an urban area with a lot of traffic."

Each bus also has space for 2 bikes at the front. Many people in Greenfield ride a bike to work. Now they can put their bike on the bus when it rains or when they are tired.

A ride typically costs $2. Students and people over 65 ride for free, but they have to show an ID. "A school ID or a library card is enough," Ms. Lee said. A bus typically comes every 20 minutes during the day and every 30 minutes in the evening.

On the first day, the line had 600 passengers. One passenger, Tom Brown, works as a nurse at the hospital. "I have been waiting for a bus like this for years," he said. "I used to drive to work, and parking was always a problem. If the bus came every 10 minutes, I would sell my car."

Another passenger, a student named Lily, said she had never taken a bus in Greenfield before. "Now I'm going to take it to school every day," she said. "It's faster than walking, and I can read on the way."

The town plans to connect 3 more streets to the line next year. "Good buses are essential in an urban area," Ms. Lee said. "They are essential for students, for workers and for older people. We want more passengers, fewer cars and cleaner air."

Questions:
What does the Number 9 bus connect?
It connects the train station with the hospital, the high school and the shopping center.
Why do the new buses produce zero smoke?
They produce zero smoke because each bus has an electric motor.
How much does a ride typically cost?
A ride typically costs $2.
What do students have to show?
They have to show an ID, for example a school ID.
How many passengers did the line have on the first day?
It had 600 passengers.
What would Tom Brown do if the bus came every 10 minutes?
He would sell his car.

lessons.title: The Ice Storm
lessons.summary: A girl writes in her diary about an ice storm that leaves her family without power for a day.
lessons.text:
Tuesday, January 14

This afternoon, the radio gave a warning about a big storm. The warning said the storm would bring strong wind, rain and ice tonight. When I looked out of the window, the sky was full of dark gray clouds. I had never seen such low, heavy clouds before.

The town put some tips on its website. Tip 1: stay at home when the storm hits. Tip 2: keep your phone charged. Tip 3: if a power wire falls down, stay far away from it, because a wire on the ground is a real danger. We charged our phones. Dad brought in extra wood for the fire.

Wednesday, January 15, very early

It's the middle of the night, and I can't sleep. The storm is here. Every time the wind hits the house, the windows shake. The lights went off an hour ago.

Wednesday, January 15, evening

When I woke up this morning, a thin layer of ice covered everything: the cars, the trees, the road and the power wires. It was beautiful, but the town said the ice was a danger, so we stayed inside. On the radio, they said that about 3,000 households had lost power. Our household was one of them.

It was cold in the house all day, so we sat by the fire, wearing 2 layers of clothes. Dad cooked soup on the fire. Mom said, "This isn't a crisis. We have food, water and warm clothes. We just have to wait." I enjoyed playing cards with my little brother. If we had power right now, we would probably watch TV. But I think cards are more fun.

Thursday, January 16

The power came back at 4 in the afternoon. Workers had been repairing the wires all night and all day. The sun came out, and the clouds were gone. The layer of ice began to melt.

The radio said that nobody in town was hurt. The mayor said the town had been ready, so the storm did not turn into a crisis. Next time, I'm going to remember the tips.

Questions:
What did the warning say?
It said the storm would bring strong wind, rain and ice.
What was the third tip?
If a power wire falls down, stay far away from it, because it is a real danger.
What covered everything in the morning?
A thin layer of ice covered everything.
How many households lost power?
About 3,000 households lost power.
Why did Mom say it wasn't a crisis?
She said it wasn't a crisis because they had food, water and warm clothes.
When did the power come back?
It came back at 4 in the afternoon on Thursday.

lessons.title: The Science Prize
lessons.summary: A twelve-year-old girl does an experiment with plants and wins the town's science contest.
lessons.text:
Every spring, the schools of Greenfield have a science contest. This year, 40 students decided to compete. Maya Patel, 12, was one of them.

Maya had always enjoyed working in the garden with her grandfather. Last summer, she had noticed something interesting: the plants near the house grew more slowly than the plants in the middle of the garden. So she decided to do an experiment about light.

For her experiment, Maya grew 3 groups of beans in small pots. The first group got light all day. The second group got light for half of the day. The third group stayed in a dark room. Every morning, Maya measured the plants and wrote the numbers in a chart. After 4 weeks, her chart showed a clear result. The beans with the most light were the tallest.

To compete in the contest, each student had to submit a short report by March 1. Maya submitted her report and her chart a week early. Then the judges made a selection. They chose 10 students out of 40 for the final. Maya was part of the selection.

At the final, each student had to demonstrate an experiment to the judges. Maya felt nervous. She didn't have much confidence. "What if I forget everything?" she asked her teacher, Mr. Ford.

"You have been working on this for months," Mr. Ford said. "If you weren't ready, you wouldn't be in the final. Just talk about your plants."

That gave Maya confidence. She showed the judges her beans and her chart, and she demonstrated how she had measured the plants. She answered every question clearly.

At the end of the day, the judges announced the winner: Maya Patel. The reward for first place was $500 for her school's science room and a visit to the state university. Maya was very happy with her reward. But the best reward, she said, was her new confidence. "Next year, I want to compete again," she said.

Questions:
How many students decided to compete in the contest?
40 students decided to compete.
What did Maya's experiment show?
It showed that the beans with the most light were the tallest.
Where did Maya write the numbers?
She wrote the numbers in a chart.
What did each student have to submit?
Each student had to submit a short report.
How did Mr. Ford give Maya confidence?
He told her that if she wasn't ready, she wouldn't be in the final.
What was the reward for first place?
It was $500 for her school's science room and a visit to the state university.

lessons.title: The Lost Dog
lessons.summary: A woman's dog runs away in the park, and a volunteer helps her find him with a safe trap.
lessons.text:
Lost Dog Found After 4 Days

Last Saturday, Emily Clark was walking her dog, Max, in Greenfield Park when a car made a loud noise. Max was afraid, and he ran into the woods. Emily called his name again and again, but Max did not come back.

Max is a small brown dog with a red band around his neck. He is usually very friendly. But when he is afraid, he hides.

Emily was very upset. She and her boyfriend, Josh, looked for Max all evening. The next day, they put up photographs of Max on trees and in shops. Josh also put a photograph of Max on the town's website.

That evening, a volunteer named Ruth Green saw the photograph on the website and called Emily. Ruth is a volunteer with a local group that helps people find lost dogs. She had already helped to find more than 50 dogs. "A dog that is afraid won't come to you, even if he is friendly," Ruth explained. "But he will come to food. We should use a trap."

Emily was still upset, and she was worried. "Will a trap hurt him?" she asked. "No," Ruth said. "It's a big box with a door. The dog walks in to eat, and the door closes behind him. It's completely safe."

That same night, Ruth put the trap at the edge of the woods, near the place where Max had run away. She put some meat inside it. Every few hours, another volunteer checked the trap. The next morning, the meat was still there. On the second morning, some of the meat was gone, but the trap was empty.

On the third morning, Ruth called again. "We have him!" she said. When Emily and Josh arrived, Max sat inside the trap. He was dirty, but he was fine. He sat quietly and ate the last piece of meat. When he saw Emily, he jumped up and tried to lick her face.

"You're an angel," Emily told Ruth. "Without you, I would still be looking for him."

Ruth only smiled. "I'm not an angel," she said. "I just love dogs."

Questions:
Why did Max run into the woods?
He ran into the woods because a car made a loud noise and he was afraid.
What does Max have around his neck?
He has a red band around his neck.
Who helped Emily put up photographs?
Her boyfriend, Josh, helped her.
Who is Ruth?
She is a volunteer with a group that helps people find lost dogs.
What did Ruth put inside the trap?
She put some meat inside the trap.
What did Emily call Ruth?
She called her an angel.

lessons.title: The Harvest Festival
lessons.summary: A local writer describes the town's yearly harvest festival, from the pancake breakfast to the evening concert.
lessons.text:
I have been going to the Greenfield Harvest Festival for 30 years, and it is still my favorite weekend of the year.

The festival has an interesting origin. In 1952, the farmers of Greenfield had a very good year, and they decided to have a party in the town square. They cooked food, played music and danced. People enjoyed it so much that they did it again the next year, and the next. That is the origin of our festival. Today, it is one of the oldest traditions in the state.

Another tradition is the color orange. Everyone wears something orange during the festival: an orange shirt or an orange hat. At the entrance, volunteers give every visitor an orange button to wear on their coat. I have kept every button since 1994. My wife says I have too many buttons.

The festival begins on Saturday morning with a big breakfast. Cooks make pancakes in huge pans on the street. Each pan is as big as a table. The smell of pancakes is everywhere.

In the afternoon, there is a cooking contest. The winner gets a paper crown and wears it for the rest of the day. This year, the crown went to Linda Moore, who made a soup with apples.

There is also ice cream. A family from the next town makes it with fresh cream from their own cows. Their apple ice cream is the best I have ever eaten. If I could eat only one thing at the festival, I would choose their ice cream.

The festival ends with a concert in the park. This year, the high school band played for an hour. The best moment of the concert was a guitar solo by a 15-year-old girl named Sara. When she finished her solo, everyone stood up. I took off my hat and waved it.

As I walked home, I thought about the farmers in 1952. They had started a small party, and it had turned into a tradition for the whole town.

Questions:
What is the origin of the festival?
In 1952, the farmers had a very good year and decided to have a party in the town square.
What do volunteers give every visitor?
They give every visitor an orange button.
How do cooks make the pancakes?
They make them in huge pans on the street.
What does the winner of the cooking contest get?
The winner gets a paper crown.
What is the ice cream made with?
It is made with fresh cream from the family's own cows.
What was the best moment of the concert?
The best moment was a guitar solo by a 15-year-old girl named Sara.

lessons.title: The New Hospital Wing
lessons.summary: Greenfield Hospital opens a new wing for surgery, paid for partly by the town's families.
lessons.text:
On Friday, Greenfield Hospital opened its new wing. The hospital first opened its doors in 1955, and this is the biggest change since then.

The new wing has modern facilities for surgery. There are 4 new rooms for surgery and 30 rooms where patients can recover after surgery. Each room has a large window and a view of the river. "Patients recover faster when they can see trees and water," said Dr. Ann Hall, who leads the hospital.

The wing was planned specifically for 2 groups of patients: children and older people. There is a play room specifically for children, and the halls have chairs where older patients can rest. In the middle of the building, there is a small internal garden with flowers and a fountain.

The new facilities will also help patients who need minor surgery. Before, people often stayed in the hospital for a night, even after a minor operation. Now, most of them can go home on the same day.

The wing cost $12 million. Most of the money came from the state, but $2 million came from contributions from numerous families and local businesses. A group of students had been selling cookies for a whole year, and they gave $800.

On the wall near the entrance, there is a long list with the names of everyone who made a contribution. "This wall is an expression of thanks," Dr. Hall said. "Numerous people helped us."

The hospital also wants to establish a group of volunteers. "We want to establish a team of people who can visit patients and talk with them," Dr. Hall said.

One of the first patients was Frank Wilson, 78. He had surgery on his knee on Monday, and he has been recovering in the new wing since then. "My room is very comfortable," he said. "If I had a room like this at home, I would never leave it." Mr. Wilson's daughter had made a contribution of $50. When he found his daughter's name on the wall, he had a happy expression on his face.

Questions:
What does the new wing have?
It has modern facilities for surgery and 30 rooms where patients can recover.
Which 2 groups of patients was the wing planned for?
It was planned specifically for children and older people.
Where is the internal garden?
It is in the middle of the building.
How much money came from contributions?
$2 million came from contributions from numerous families and local businesses.
What is the wall near the entrance?
It is an expression of thanks to everyone who made a contribution.
What kind of group does the hospital want to establish?
It wants to establish a group of volunteers who can visit patients.

lessons.title: The Old Mill
lessons.summary: The town discusses two proposals for an empty mill by the river and votes to turn it into a community center.
lessons.text:
The old mill on Greenfield River is the oldest building in town. It was built in 1870. For 100 years, it was a factory that made paper. In 1980, the factory closed, and the mill has been empty since then.

This year, the town council received 2 proposals for the mill. The first proposal came from a large company. The company wanted to turn the mill into corporate offices for 200 workers. The second proposal came from a group of local people. They wanted to turn the mill into a community center with a library, a café and rooms for classes.

Before the council made a decision, it held a public meeting in the assembly hall of the high school. More than 300 people came to the assembly. Opinions varied a lot. Some people liked the corporate proposal. "200 new jobs would be good for our shops and restaurants," a shop owner said. Others preferred the community center. "The mill belongs to the town's history," a teacher said. "It should be a place for everyone."

At the assembly, people also spoke from different perspectives. From the perspective of young families, a library and classes were the most important things. From the perspective of business owners, jobs were more important. A man who had worked at the paper factory for 30 years spoke, too. "From my perspective, I just want the mill to be full of people again," he said.

The local newspaper also did a poll. In the poll, 64 percent of readers chose the community center, and 36 percent chose the corporate offices. The results of the poll varied by age: younger readers were more interested in the jobs.

In the end, the council passed a resolution. The resolution said that the mill would become a community center. However, the council also promised to help the company find another building in town. "We are committed to creating jobs," the mayor said. "And we are also committed to protecting our history."

Work on the old mill will begin in the spring.

Questions:
What was the mill for 100 years?
It was a factory that made paper.
What were the 2 proposals?
The first proposal was for corporate offices, and the second was for a community center.
Where did the town hold the public meeting?
It held the meeting in the assembly hall of the high school.
What did the man who had worked at the factory want?
He wanted the mill to be full of people again.
What did the poll show?
64 percent of readers chose the community center, and 36 percent chose the corporate offices.
What did the resolution say?
It said that the mill would become a community center.

lessons.title: Better School Lunches
lessons.summary: A school cook writes to the local newspaper about the new, healthier lunches at Greenfield schools.
lessons.text:
A Letter to the Greenfield News

Dear Editor,

My name is Rosa Diaz, and I have been working as a cook at Greenfield Middle School for 12 years. I am writing to tell your readers about the changes in our school lunches this year.

Last year, the town did an assessment of all school meals. A team of doctors and cooks looked at every meal for a month. The assessment revealed 2 problems. First, our meals had too much salt. Second, many meals did not have enough protein. Protein is important for growing children, because it helps them build strong bodies. The assessment also revealed that many students were drinking soda with their lunch.

After the assessment, we decided to introduce new meals step by step. We started to use less salt and more fresh herbs. We started to serve more fish, chicken, eggs and beans, which are good sources of protein. Instead of soda, we now serve water, milk and pure fruit juice with no added sugar. We also offer a broad selection of fruit and vegetables every day. The selection is so broad that every student can find something they like.

At first, some students thought the new food was odd. "This soup tastes odd," one boy told me in September. "Where is the salt?" It felt odd for me too, at the beginning. I had been cooking the same meals for years. But I kept going, and slowly things changed.

Now, in March, the same boy asks for a second bowl of soup. Less food comes back to the kitchen. The teachers say that students have more energy in the afternoon. If I could change one more thing, I would give students more time to eat. 20 minutes is too short for a good meal.

Next year, we are going to introduce a cooking class for students. I want to thank the parents who supported us. Making healthy meals is hard work, but it is worth it.

Rosa Diaz
Greenfield

Questions:
How long has Rosa Diaz been working as a cook?
She has been working as a cook for 12 years.
What did the assessment reveal?
It revealed that the meals had too much salt and not enough protein.
Why is protein important for children?
It is important because it helps them build strong bodies.
What do students drink instead of soda now?
They drink water, milk and pure fruit juice.
What did one boy think about the soup in September?
He thought the soup tasted odd.
What would Rosa change if she could change one more thing?
She would give students more time to eat.

lessons.title: Summer Reading at the Library
lessons.summary: A librarian writes to parents about a summer reading program with a different theme every week.
lessons.text:
Dear Parents,

Summer is almost here, and Greenfield Library is starting its summer reading program for children aged 7 to 12. For 4 weeks in July, children will meet at the library every Tuesday and Thursday morning. Each week, we will explore a different theme.

In week 1, we will explore the world of kings and queens. Children will read stories about a kingdom far away, and they will draw a map of their own kingdom. In week 2, the theme is friendly monsters. We will read books about funny monsters who are afraid of the dark, and each child will make a monster from paper.

In week 3, we will travel back to Roman times. Children will learn how Roman children lived, what they ate and what games they played. In week 4, we will learn about the American Revolution. A teacher from the high school will visit and tell the story of the Revolution in a simple way.

For the history weeks, we will also teach some useful skills. Children will learn how to use the index of a book. The index is at the back of the book, and it helps you find a topic quickly. If you wanted to find the word "Roman" in a big history book, you would look in the index first. We will also explain the context of each story: when it happened, where it happened and why. When children know the context, they understand a story much better.

This year, we have many new books. The youth ministry of First Church on Elm Street has been collecting books since January, and they gave 300 books to the library. We are very thankful to the youth ministry for their help.

At the end of the program, every child will get a certificate and a free book to take home.

I have worked at this library for 15 years. My belief is simple: every child can love reading. It is a belief that has grown stronger every summer.

You can sign up your child at the front desk. You will need your library card.

See you in July!

Helen Baker
Children's Librarian, Greenfield Library

Questions:
How often will the children meet at the library?
They will meet every Tuesday and Thursday morning.
What will children draw in week 1?
They will draw a map of their own kingdom.
What will each child make in week 2?
Each child will make a monster from paper.
What will children learn about in week 4?
They will learn about the American Revolution.
Where is the index of a book?
The index is at the back of the book.
Who gave 300 books to the library?
The youth ministry of First Church gave them.

lessons.title: The New Stadium
lessons.summary: A high school student writes to his grandfather about the opening game at the town's new stadium.
lessons.text:
Dear Grandpa,

I'm writing to tell you about last Saturday. It was the opening day of the new baseball stadium at Greenfield High School. I'm sorry you couldn't come, so here is everything that happened.

The old field didn't have any real seats. People had to stand or bring their own chairs. The new stadium has 3,000 seats, and they are very comfortable. There are also 4 tall light towers, one in each corner. With the light towers, the team can now play in the evening. When the lights on the towers came on, everyone cheered.

The stadium was full. There were people everywhere: on the seats, near the gates and even on the hill behind the field. Everywhere I looked, I saw our team's colors, green and white.

Before the game, the mayor gave a brief speech. It really was brief: she spoke for only 2 minutes. She thanked the workers who had built the stadium. Then the coach gave an even shorter speech. He just said, "Let's play!"

Then a small, old aircraft flew over the stadium. A pilot from the local flying club had painted the aircraft green and white for the day. People everywhere looked up and waved. Dad said it was the same kind of aircraft that he had seen at the air show when he was a boy.

After that, it was time for the first pitch. The coach asked me to throw it! I had been practicing all week, but I was still nervous. My pitch was not very fast, but it was straight, and everyone clapped. Then our best player threw the first real pitch of the game.

We won the game 5 to 3. If you came to visit in May, we could go to a game together. I would save you the most comfortable seat in the stadium.

Love,
Danny

Questions:
How many seats does the new stadium have?
It has 3,000 seats.
Why are the light towers important?
With the light towers, the team can play in the evening.
How long was the mayor's speech?
It was very brief: she spoke for only 2 minutes.
What color was the aircraft?
It was green and white.
Who threw the first pitch?
Danny threw the first pitch.
What was the result of the game?
Greenfield won the game 5 to 3.
